Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Sparse diagonal stroke continuation

## When to use
Use when an ARC grid has a mostly uniform background and compact sparse motifs that may encode diagonal lines extended to grid boundaries. This is a class-level hypothesis workflow, not an ID-specific answer recipe.

## Workflow
1. Record all non-background coordinates and group by color. Separate same-color aligned pairs/segments from isolated cells and from mixed-color diagonal chains.
2. For each plausible same-color segment, test both diagonal orientations (down-right/up-left and down-left/up-right). Identify segment endpoints and compute exact ray cells to boundaries without altering the seed.
3. Compare each prediction against every demo output. Record which colors/segments extend, which directions fire, and which plausible near-matches are unchanged. Do not infer that every diagonal pair activates.
4. Apply only the demonstrated selector and ray paths to the test. Preserve other cells and seed colors unless outputs explicitly change them. Mechanically validate dimensions and coordinate indices.
5. After incorrect feedback, reject that hypothesis and identify the alternative selector distinction; do not repeat a similar output with minor transcription changes.

## Pitfalls
- Mixed-color objects can resemble a diagonal run; require same-color evidence unless demos show otherwise.
- Extending all same-color diagonal segments is not established merely because one demo extends a pair. A test submission extending both a 9 diagonal pair and a separate 1 pair was rejected. Selector behavior was not fully revealed.

- Stroke endpoints may already contain multiple seed cells; preserve every original seed cell and extend outward from the correct endpoint rather than overwriting or filling the whole diagonal indiscriminately.

## Evidence
Demo 1 had background 6 and shape color 7. The salient compact 7 frame-like pattern (rows 10–11 and 27–29, columns 4–10) remained unchanged. Some other sparse 7 cells were recolored to 2, while other sparse cells remained unchanged. The exact test instance had background 5 and object color 0.

Recolor the following eight background-5 cells to 2; preserve every other cell:
- (r2,c3), (r3,c3), (r3,c9)
- (r5,c3), (r7,c3)

# task-37f0b9db: fill gaps between same-row/column markers

## Verified rule
Given a sparse grid with uniform background and marker color 1 or 7 (palette varies), place color 3 in every background cell strictly between consecutive marker cells on any common row or common column. Preserve the original markers and all other cells. Each direction is computed from the original marker locations; gaps between consecutive markers are filled, while cells outside the first/last markers on a line remain unchanged. Horizontal and vertical fills combine. If horizontal/vertical fill intersect, the cell remains 3.

## Demo evidence
Demo input 10x11: background 9, markers 1. Output fills color 3 strictly between consecutive markers on each row and column. Examples: row 1 markers at c4,c9 fill c5-c8; row 5 markers c0,c9 fill c1-c8; column 4 has markers at r1,r7 filling r2-r6; column 0 markers r5,r9 fill r6-r8. Original 1 markers remain untouched. Other positions stay 9.

## Verified test result
Task test was 28x11, background 1, marker 7. Filled all strictly intermediate cells between consecutive 7 markers horizontally/vertically in color 3, preserving all original 7 and remaining 1. The resulting grid was accepted with zero incorrect submissions.

## Procedure / pitfalls
1. On each row, list columns whose original value is the marker; fill cells strictly between each neighboring pair with 3.
2. On each column, do the same for marker rows.
3. Do not fill before first/after last marker, nor all background across a line unless bracketed by two consecutive markers.
4. Preserve marker cells. Identify actual background/marker colors per instance; output fill color is 3 per evidence.
5. Apply horizontal and vertical passes based on original markers, never treat newly filled cells as markers."
}
